## What the bug was
In `call_command()` (`django/core/management/__init__.py`), kwargs were only forwarded to `parse_args()` for options with `opt.required == True`. Members of a **required mutually exclusive group** individually have `required=False` — the requirement lives on the group — so `call_command('my_command', shop_id=1)` never passed `--shop-id=1` to the parser, and argparse raised `Error: one of the arguments --shop-id --shop is required`.

## The fix (minimal, source-only, matches upstream Django commit `6c379f1a18` "Fixed #30763")
In `call_command()`, collect the members of required mutually exclusive groups and treat them like required options:

```python
mutually_exclusive_required_options = {
    opt
    for group in parser._mutually_exclusive_groups
    for opt in group._group_actions if group.required
}
parse_args += [
    '{}={}'.format(min(opt.option_strings), arg_options[opt.dest])
    for opt in parser_actions if (
        opt.dest in options and
        (opt.required or opt in mutually_exclusive_required_options)
    )
]
```
